title: On successful completion the upload surface renders an assertive-slot announcement and per-file remove and retry controls
asA: operator whose upload set has just finished
iWant: an assertive-slot announcement saying how many files uploaded successfully, plus a keyboard-reachable remove control per completed file
soThat: my screen reader tells me the set is done and I can remove a file I no longer want without a page reload

acceptanceCriteria.description: After the fixture completes the upload set the upload region carries a [data-assertive-slot] element with aria-live="assertive" or role="status" whose textContent matches /^\d+ files uploaded successfully$/, each completed file row carries [data-file-row][data-file-state="complete"], a keyboard-reachable [data-recovery="remove"] button per row and, after a refused-then-succeeded row, a [data-recovery="retry"] button visible only until the retry succeeds.

On successful removal (the transport DELETE returns 204 or a defined 200), the upload surface removes the row, announces the removal via the polite live region and no upload artefact remains referenced in the applied data blueprint.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a completed upload row and a successful DELETE
acceptanceCriteria.then: the row is removed from the DOM, a polite announcement fires and the applied data blueprint no longer references the artefact

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the transport DELETE returns a non-2xx or times out, the row remains with data-remove-outcome=failed, the assertive live region announces the failure, no recovery artefact is deleted downstream, and a retry stays keyboard-reachable.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a completed upload row and a DELETE that returns a non-2xx or times out
acceptanceCriteria.then: the row remains with data-remove-outcome=failed, the assertive live region announces the failure and a retry is keyboard-reachable

acceptanceCriteria.description: The completion once contract: a single upload emits exactly one completion announcement even under a retry; two rapid completions from the same upload id emit one announcement (idempotency of a retried operation).
acceptanceCriteria.given: an upload that emits two completion events for the same upload id
acceptanceCriteria.then: exactly one completion announcement fires and no duplicate data-complete=true is emitted
